clue.text: Some youth misbehaving peers concealed

indicators.note: letters that misbehave will not stay in their proper order, so the fodder is rearranged

blocks.note: the two words used letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Some unruly youngsters get up to mischief their peers keep hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because the years just before the teens are one part of a person's youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Preadolescence is the stage of childhood just before puberty, a portion of the period of youth.

clue.text: Benefactor giving disorganised hospital PR hint

indicators.note: something disorganised lacks order, so the fodder letters are to be put in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the three words used letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A donor helps a chaotic hospital by tipping off its publicity department.
explanation.definitionFit: A philanthropist is a person who gives money to good causes, which is what a benefactor does.

clue.text: Take advantage of mine no longer, having left nothing inside

indicators.note: inside says the following letters are placed within the word for a mine

blocks.note: ex- means former, no longer
a pit is a coal mine
L is the abbreviation for left
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A closed mine, abandoned with nothing left in it, is no longer worth exploiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like 'remaining' but is the abbreviation L, and 'nothing' is the letter O; together they go inside the mine.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to make use of it for gain, a direct synonym of taking advantage of it.

clue.text: Strangely considerate, doing harm to something sacred

indicators.note: strangely says the next word's letters appear in an odd, unexpected order

blocks.note: the fodder, used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone oddly polite while vandalising a holy place.
explanation.definitionFit: Desecration is the act of violating or damaging a holy place or object, so a noun for harming the sacred.

clue.text: Use bottom bunk, perhaps, to avoid detection

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: sleep in the lower bed of a bunk
second meaning: the idiom for keeping out of sight

explanation.surface: A fugitive hides by sleeping in the lower bunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' flags that the bottom bunk is just one example of the literal sense; the idiom is the real definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is an idiom for staying hidden and quiet; literally, someone in a bottom bunk lies in a low position.

clue.text: Shown on TV? Not viewable

blocks.note: first meaning: broadcast on a screen
second meaning: hidden behind a screen

explanation.walkthrough: The two definitions are near opposites, which is the joke: one sense of the word puts it on a screen, the other hides it behind one.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme screened is broadcast; something screened off is concealed behind a partition, so both senses come from the same past participle.

clue.text: Taking part in travel, maybe, one has a trunk and leaves

definitions.text: one has a trunk and leaves

indicators.note: taking part in means the answer is a part of the following words, sitting within them

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A traveller packs a trunk and sets off.
explanation.walkthrough: The trunk and leaves sound like luggage and departure; they are a tree's stem and foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: An elm is a tree, and every tree has a trunk and leaves.

clue.text: Communication from Tory short time before piece of legislation

indicators.note: before places one piece ahead of the next in the down entry

blocks.note: Con is short for Conservative, the party of the Tories
T is the short form of time
an act is a law passed by parliament

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician sends a quick message just before a bill becomes law.
explanation.definitionFit: Contact means communication between people, as in 'we have had no contact'.

clue.text: Blazing revolver?

blocks.note: surface reading: a gun firing away in a shootout
setter's reading: something that spins round while burning, a pinned firework

explanation.walkthrough: A revolver suggests a pistol and blazing suggests gunfire; here it is anything that revolves, and it is literally on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catherine wheel is a firework nailed to a post that spins while it burns, named after St Catherine's martyrdom wheel.

clue.text: Deadlock that is broken by person elected ahead of idiot

indicators.note: ahead of puts the word for an elected person in front of the word for a fool
something broken by another thing is split open with that thing sitting in the gap

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a Member of Parliament is elected
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A political stalemate is ended when a new MP takes precedence over a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a situation where no progress is possible, the same standstill as a deadlock.

clue.text: Country's troops in retreat — madness!

indicators.note: troops in retreat go back the way they came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
mania is wild madness

explanation.surface: A nation's army falls back in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is the crossword convention for ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a nation in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Capital I extracted from villain in past

indicators.note: something extracted is pulled out and removed, so that letter goes

blocks.note: Iago is the schemer in Shakespeare's Othello
an upper-case letter I, the one taken away

explanation.surface: A major crook was jailed and moved out of the city years back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital I' reads like a city name; it just means the letter I in upper case, removed from IAGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago refers to a time before now, as in 'two years ago', which places something in the past.

clue.text: Wrongly charge poor husband — specify steps to be performed

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters that follow are set out incorrectly and must be put right

blocks.note: fodder, letter for letter
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: An unjust accusation of a needy man is laid out step by step.
explanation.definitionFit: To choreograph is to plan the sequence of movements in a dance, setting out the moves dancers will perform.

clue.text: Muck-raking journalists, say, surrounded by good crowd

indicators.note: surrounded by means the word for speaking sits between the other two pieces

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a press is a dense crowd of people
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Scandal-hungry reporters are mobbed by a well-behaved crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is a verb meaning speak; the crowd and the good split around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The gutter press is a disparaging term for sensational tabloid newspapers that dig up scandal.

clue.text: Italian repeatedly turned to an artist from Venice

indicators.note: turned means turned around, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: IT is short for Italian (as in gin and it), taken twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian keeps turning to look at a Venetian painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Renaissance painter of the Venetian school.

clue.text: Will producer try out actor clubs rejected?

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown out, so the card suit letter is removed from the word for performer

blocks.note: to test is to try out
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for the card suit clubs

explanation.surface: Will a film producer audition a performer the clubs have turned down?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' seems to begin a question; it is a legal will, and its producer is the person who makes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is the person who makes a legal will, so a cryptic 'will producer'.

clue.text: Gives birth to family — hence hide from wild animal

blocks.note: to bear a child is to give birth to it
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A mother delivers children and so hides her family from a wild beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb but is the noun: an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearskin is the pelt of a bear, a wild animal's hide.

clue.text: A rentier arranged for payment in advance

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the fodder letters are reordered

blocks.note: fodder, letter for letter

explanation.surface: A person living off rents sets up a payment up front.
explanation.walkthrough: A rentier is someone whose income comes from property or investments.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is a fee paid in advance to secure someone's services, such as a lawyer's.

clue.text: Major storm created by fuss over rent? Just the opposite

blocks.note: rent as the past tense of rend, torn
ado is fuss
no letters: an instruction to swap the order 'fuss over rent' describes

explanation.surface: A huge row blows up over a dispute about rent.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken straight, fuss over rent puts ADO above TORN in a down entry; 'Just the opposite' swaps them so TORN comes first. 'Rent' means torn, not money paid to a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm, one of the most severe kinds of storm.

clue.text: Get back, for example, into shower

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a shower is a spell of rain
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Someone tells another to go back into the shower.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain something is to recover it after losing it, a synonym of getting it back.

clue.text: Like some wines containing sulphur he never imbibes

definitions.note: the answer as a noun: a person of self-denial, here one who never drinks

indicators.note: containing says the word for vinegary wines holds the next letter inside it

blocks.note: wine gone off turns vinegary, which is acetic
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A teetotaller avoids wines because of their sulphite content.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic is someone who practises strict self-denial, giving up pleasures such as alcohol.

clue.text: Showing virtue of kind hard to be found in social group

indicators.note: to be found in places one letter inside the word for the group

blocks.note: a caste is a hereditary social class
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A rare kind of goodness is hard to come by in high society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of kind' makes the definition specific: one particular kind of virtue, purity.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means sexually pure or abstinent, a particular moral virtue.

clue.text: Stand firm with at least two top people

definitions.text: firm with at least two top people

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket, a stand is a run-scoring spell by two batsmen together

blocks.clueFragment: firm with at least two top people
blocks.note: second meaning: a business owned and run by two or more equal principals

explanation.surface: A boss tells a pair of senior colleagues to hold their ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand firm' reads as one phrase meaning refuse to yield; split it. In cricket, a stand is the runs two batsmen add together while both are in.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a stand is also called a batting partnership, and a business owned jointly by two or more partners is likewise a partnership.

clue.text: Intimidate female whose homecoming is indefinitely delayed

definitions.text: female whose homecoming is indefinitely delayed

blocks.note: first meaning: to bully into submission

blocks.clueFragment: female whose homecoming is indefinitely delayed
blocks.note: second meaning: from the idiom 'till they come home', meaning forever

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the phrase 'until the cows come home', meaning for an indefinitely long time.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to frighten them into submission; a cow is the female of cattle, famously never home in the idiom.

clue.text: Get mildly angry, so to speak, in plant

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the words are to be heard rather than read as spelt

blocks.note: to see red is to get angry, so a milder shade is a gentler fury

explanation.surface: A gardener gets a little cross with a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay invents a milder version of the idiom 'see red'; the first word then sounds like the spelling the plant uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea pink is another name for thrift, a coastal plant with pink flowers.

clue.text: Mass, following one's specific doctrine

indicators.note: following places the word for a church service after the other piece

blocks.note: one is I, and 's is a contraction of is
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Attending Mass after following one's own particular creed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests the church service, but it is the physics abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is any distinctive doctrine or theory, as in the suffix of words like Marxism.

clue.text: Unorthodox religious group penning page about ghost

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the group's word holds the next letter

blocks.note: a sect is a breakaway religious group
P is the abbreviation for page
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A fringe cult is writing a book about a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is an apparition or phantom, another word for a ghost.

clue.text: Down-to-earth sons men upset? Funny about that

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters before it are jumbled
about means going around, so the word for funny wraps the jumbled letters

blocks.note: comical means funny
fodder, letter for letter

explanation.surface: Practical sons upset the men; is that funny?
explanation.definitionFit: Commonsensical means having practical good judgement, which is what a down-to-earth person shows.
